title: Welcome to ρ = 0
text:
This blog is moving here from WordPress. Future posts will mix research findings, data visualization, and the occasional uncorrelated tangent.
Posts can contain live R code. A chunk like the one below runs when the post is rendered, and its output is cached so it doesn’t rerun unless the post changes:
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#970909") +
  theme_minimal()
(Write it as {r} instead of r after the backticks to make it execute.)

title: Research
text: How do respiratory viruses move between places and populations? Using genomic data we can track transmission chains and then infer how these viruses spread. In particular, I am excited to study how human movement across populations influences the spread of epidemics. This knowledge is important for designing public health interventions to block transmission and construct pathogen surveillance networks to capture genomic and population changes.

title: Research
text:
Within-host viral dynamics
Mathematical models of viral replication and immune control are exciting tools to describe the course of infections in individuals. Models can additionally be used to predict how infections respond to therapeutics (e.g. mAbs and antivirals) and how pathogens evolve within hosts. My goal is to use these models to understand how respiratory viruses develop novel variants especially under new evolutionary pressures.

title: Research
text:
Spatial epidemiology of health outcomes
Space and movement imapct the health of individuals and populations by affecting their exposures (e.g. pathogens, environmental factors, social determinants) and physical access to healthcare. My doctoral and residency research training focused on studying geospatial patterns in health outcomes including cancer mortality and vaccination uptake. I continue to be interested in pursuing questions at the intersection of geography and health.

title: Amin Bemanian, MD PhD
text:
Welcome! I am a pediatric infectious diseases physician at the University of Washington /Seattle Children’s Hospital and a research associate at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in the Schiffer and Bedford labs. My research sits at the intersection of genomic epidemiology, infectious disease modeling, and public health. I study the spread of viruses and other infectious diseases, and my goal is to better understand how pathogens evolve and adapt in response to public health interventions. My work currently is focused on respiratory viruses such as RSV and SARS-CoV-2, and I have previously investigated spatial disparities in health outcomes. Ultimately, my goal as a researcher is to use mathematics and statistics to improve the health of populations, and I am excited to collaborate on projects towards the goal.
This site houses much of my research and papers, with links to code where available. Open and reproducible research is very important to me, so please reach out if there are any questions regarding my methods or code. My blog ρ = 0 carries posts regarding data science, statistics, and medicine, that may be “uncorrelated” to my research. Expect anything there, from cool papers I am excited about to using regression models to vent about the Chicago Bulls. Feel free to email me if you have any questions about my work or ideas for collaboration.
